why: mint the root node tag vocabulary for the tag backfill

ops.title: Tags
ops.description: The root node tag dictionary: each term that records here may carry, with the one sentence saying what a record must be about to earn it
ops.body:
## in-game-testing

A record earns this term when it is about testing a mod inside the running game with TestRunner and its [OniTest] coroutines.

## test-pacing

A record earns this term when it is about spacing a test's steps in game time so the game's simulation keeps up with them.

## test-cleanup

A record earns this term when it is about how a test's area and changes are cleared or restored so tests do not affect each other.

## test-assertions

A record earns this term when it is about what a test checks and how it states the expected result.

## simulated-input

A record earns this term when it is about driving the game's real tools and screens with mouse and key input fed by a test.

## generated-worlds

A record earns this term when it is about running the game's world generation from a coordinate to produce a fresh world.

## save-files

A record earns this term when it is about Oxygen Not Included save files and what is loaded from or written to them.

## screenshots

A record earns this term when it is about photographing the game from a test run to produce images to look at.

## mod-compatibility

A record earns this term when it is about a mod working correctly alongside other authors' mods installed in the same game.

## mod-loadout

A record earns this term when it is about which mods the game has enabled and putting the player's own mod list back afterwards.

## game-update-compatibility

A record earns this term when it is about keeping mods and their tests working after a game update changes the game's own code.

## player-log

A record earns this term when it is about reading the game's Player.log to find out what went wrong in a run.

## machine-setup

A record earns this term when it is about what the owner's machine must have installed, running or configured for builds and test runs to work.

## mod-build

A record earns this term when it is about compiling the mods with dotnet against the game's assemblies and deploying them into the game's mods folder.

## common-submodule

A record earns this term when it is about the common git submodule and keeping the root repository's pointer to it in step.

## translations

A record earns this term when it is about translating a mod's player-visible strings and checking its translation files.

## release-process

A record earns this term when it is about cutting a release of a mod, from version bump and tag to the published download.

## steam-workshop

A record earns this term when it is about publishing a mod to its Steam Workshop item or updating that item.

## changelog

A record earns this term when it is about a mod's CHANGELOG.md and the player-facing release notes written in it.

## github-issues

A record earns this term when it is about the issues players file on the GitHub repository and how those issues are labelled.

## commit-messages

A record earns this term when it is about how a commit's message is worded in this repository.

## assistant-attribution

A record earns this term when it is about the trailer lines that credit an AI assistant on commits and pull requests.

## git-branches

A record earns this term when it is about the repository's git branches, how they are named and how work returns to main.

## task-id

A record earns this term when it is about the OM-NNN identifier given to an ICON task and where that identifier is used.

## task-plan

A record earns this term when it is about the plan.md that carries an ICON task through its phases.

## phase-handoff

A record earns this term when it is about entering or leaving a task-plan phase and the handoff block and commit that mark the boundary.

## unit-spec

A record earns this term when it is about the spec a manager writes for a delegated unit of work and how that unit is dispatched to a sub-agent.

## code-review

A record earns this term when it is about reviewing a change's diff before the work is reported done or merged.

## knowledge-store

A record earns this term when it is about the .context knowledge store and how records in it are written and read with ICON's ks engine.
